decisions.title: Tune effort first; send only checkable work to Haiku
decisions.context: Anthropic's own test of Haiku subagents under Opus saved 32% of cost for about 4 points of pass rate, which lowering effort also buys. Haiku 5.5 at low effort in long prompts is more likely to skip a check (research report sections 1.1, 1.2).
decisions.decision: Easy tier: Haiku 5.5 at low effort, medium over about 50k tokens. Normal: Sonnet medium. Hard: Opus high. Long: Fable unchanged. Haiku gets only mechanical work with a cheap check.
decisions.consequences: Savings come from the routine bulk. A Haiku mistake is caught by the cheap check or by a rescue; nothing silent goes to Haiku. Values are constants in hooks/lib/pricing.ts and revert with git.
decisions.decided_by: Brian asked for Haiku and a reasoning level ("haiku in some places also and the reaosnign level"); the values are inferred by agent from the research

decisions.title: Judging agents never run on Haiku
decisions.context: A wrong review, plan or answer is a silent error that a cheap check does not catch, and downstream work builds on it (research report section 4).
decisions.decision: Agent types architect, Plan, reviewer, code-review, project-brain, researcher and *-reviewer get the judge limits: Sonnet or higher, and pace or rate-limit pressure cannot lower them below Sonnet.
decisions.consequences: Some review runs cost more than a Haiku would. The match is on the agent type name, not task prose.
decisions.decided_by: inferred by agent from the research; Brian's brief: design, review and anything he reads never go to Haiku

decisions.title: Build no hook for the main-conversation model
decisions.context: The research found no plugin mechanism that sets the main session's model or effort (section 1.4), with a coverage gap tracked as Q4.
decisions.decision: Record the lever in the README (settings default plus /model and /effort) and show the main-conversation cost in the daily report instead.
decisions.consequences: The main model stays a manual lever; if Q4 finds a mechanism, this decision is revisited.
decisions.decided_by: Brian's instruction on #162 (item 1: build no hook)

decisions.title: Feedback from existing logs, proposals as recorded decisions
decisions.context: The router keeps no log of its own; the transcripts and the daily report already hold what is needed.
decisions.decision: Add an outcome per run to the daily report and a Monday weekly review that groups outcomes by agent type and tier and proposes decisions; a session accepts or rejects each after reading the traces.
decisions.consequences: Signals catch loud failure only (Q2). Raise a tier at 10+ runs and 12%+ bad; lower at 30+ runs and under 3%, never for judging agents. Thresholds are inferred by agent.
decisions.decided_by: Brian asked for a feedback system so it improves over time; thresholds inferred by agent
